sections.h2: Where do I take property tax questions in Pope County?
sections.html:
Both property tax offices sit in the courthouse at 130 E. Minnesota Avenue in Glenwood. The Assessor, at 320-634-7715, sets the estimated market value and the class of each parcel. The Auditor/Treasurer, at 320-634-7706, prepares and mails the statements, takes payments and manages delinquent accounts. The Auditor/Treasurer's page puts the yearly mailing at more than 13,500 real estate and mobile home statements and the amount collected at over $14,000,000.

The Auditor/Treasurer is an elected post, and the office keeps weekday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The same counter handles a change of taxpayer name or address, an ACH form for twice-a-year automatic withdrawal, and the sale of tax-forfeited land.

Sellers usually need both offices. The Assessor explains a value or a homestead question, and the Auditor/Treasurer supplies the balance that must be cleared before a deed can move.

sections.h2: What is Pope County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Pope County is farm and lake country in west central Minnesota. It covers 717 square miles, with 670 of land and 47 of water, and its terrain is low rolling hills dotted with ponds. The Chippewa River runs through the western side, and Lake Minnewaska, Lake Emily and Lake Johanna are among the better-known waters. Glacial Lakes State Park is among the protected areas.

Glenwood is the county seat and largest city. Starbuck, Villard, Lowry, Cyrus, Farwell, Long Beach, Sedan, Westport and part of Brooten complete the list of cities. The county was identified by the legislature in 1862, named for General John Pope, and organized in 1866. Its 1930 Beaux-Arts courthouse is on the National Register of Historic Places.

From Census Bureau QuickFacts:

  • 11,420 residents on July 1, 2025, a 1.0% gain since 2020
  • 6,549 housing units, with 83.5% occupied by owners
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home of $255,100 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median household income of $76,220 and a 22.7 minute average drive to work
  • Only 33 building permits in 2025, and 27.5% of residents aged 65 or older

With few new homes being built, resale sellers here are often handling a parent's house or a lake property with an older owner.

sections.h2: What is happening with the Pope County 2027 levy?
sections.html:
On September 15, 2026 the County Board set a preliminary 2027 levy of $11,809,106, which is 3.4% above the 2026 levy of $11,420,799. State law lets the county hold or lower that figure at final adoption but not raise it. The county notes that its levy has averaged a 2.2% yearly increase since 2017, with a low of a 3.0% cut in 2021 and a high of a 6.9% rise in 2024.

The Truth-in-Taxation hearing is scheduled for Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. at the courthouse, so it is still ahead. Each parcel gets a single proposed-tax notice from the Auditor/Treasurer, but the county reminds owners that it decides only the county line. City, township, school and special district proposals have their own hearings, and those dates are printed on the notice. The 2027 budget also includes a one-time $1,950,000 draw from road and bridge fund balance.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pope County valuation?
sections.html:
The county tells owners that spring is the moment to act, when the valuation notice arrives with the tax statement. By the time proposed taxes come out in the fall it is too late. The usual route has these stops:

  • Call the Assessor at 320-634-7715 and discuss the value or class informally. The county's tax timeline says informal appeals run until the special County Board meeting in early June.
  • Go to your local board of appeal and equalization. Local meetings are by appointment through the Assessor. In 2026, for example, the Glenwood open book session ran at the Assessor's Office at 9:00 a.m. on April 20, and Rolling Forks Township met at its town hall on April 22.
  • Appear before the County Board of Appeal and Equalization. In 2026 it met at 6:30 p.m. on June 15 in the courthouse board room, and speakers needed an appointment made by June 10.

The county's appeals FAQ adds a warning that state law puts the burden of proof on the owner. Your evidence has to be strong enough to show the Assessor's number is wrong, and only relevant testimony given at the board counts.

sections.h2: When are Pope County property taxes due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is paid in halves, with the first due May 15 and the second due October 15. The second half on class 2a agricultural land is not due until November 15. Pope County does not mail second-half statements, so the stub from the spring mailing is what you send back in the fall. Taxes of $100 or less must be paid in full with the first half.

The county's 2026 statement lists the penalty ladder for homestead and cabin property:

Nonhomestead land carries double the early rates, starting at 4% after May 15. The statement also says the office cannot accept post-dated checks, that a postmark from the Postal Service proves timely mailing, and that a private meter postmark does not.

sections.h2: What else shows up on a Pope County tax statement?
sections.html:
Bills here include a solid waste fee. The 2026 payable-year fee was $139 on any property with a building value of $5,000 or more, collected for the Pope/Douglas Solid Waste Management system at 320-763-9340. It is a charge listed apart from the value-based tax.

The homestead exclusion works as a reduction of taxable value. On the 2026 statement it peaks at $38,000 for a home valued at $95,000, shrinks by nine percent of the value above that, and disappears at $517,200. Special assessments for streets, sidewalks and sewers appear in their own section, and the county notes they are based on benefit to the property, not market value.

Many bills are paid through a lender's escrow account. The county mails the owner a copy anyway and sends the lender its own listing.

sections.h2: What tax relief can a Pope County owner use, and what happens when the house sells?
sections.html:
The statement describes two state refunds for homesteads owned and occupied on January 2. The regular refund applies when taxes exceed income-based thresholds and household income is under $142,490. The special refund applies when net tax on the homestead rose more than 12% and the increase was at least $100. Both use Form M1PR, due August 15. A senior deferral is also offered for owners 65 or older with household income of $96,000 or less who have lived in the home five years; the filing date for 2027 was November 1, 2026, so a new applicant would look at next year.

Sellers should ask the Auditor/Treasurer for a payoff before listing. If the property is a mobile home, the county's ownership-change form requires the entire parcel's taxes to be paid, and both the Auditor/Treasurer and the Assessor must sign before the Department of Motor Vehicles can transfer the title.

faqs.q: What number do I call to dispute a Pope County property value?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office at 320-634-7715. Call before the early June special board meeting for an informal review, and make an appointment if you plan to speak at the County Board of Appeal and Equalization.

faqs.q: Does Pope County mail a bill for the second half?
faqs.a: No. The Auditor/Treasurer states that second-half statements are not mailed. Use the second-half stub from the statement you received in the spring, and mail it or bring it in by October 15.

faqs.q: What is the Pope County solid waste fee?
faqs.a: It is a charge on properties with a building value of $5,000 or more that supports the Pope/Douglas Solid Waste Management system. It was $139 for the 2026 taxes payable year. Call 320-763-9340 with questions about the fee.

faqs.q: Is the Pope County Truth-in-Taxation hearing coming up?
faqs.a: Yes. The county hearing is Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. at the courthouse in Glenwood. Other taxing bodies hold separate hearings listed on your proposed notice.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pope County property tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes, through the ACH Real Estate Tax Payment Form on the Auditor/Treasurer's page. It deducts payments from a checking or savings account twice a year. Return the completed form to the office.
